title: Visual asset guardrails for onboarding screenshots
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Establish a repeatable, brand-consistent pipeline and lightweight tooling to produce privacy-safe, localization-ready UI screenshots and short GIFs for onboarding/quickstart docs and release pages. Deliverables: (1) a visual spec and export presets (crop/aspect/safe area, margin, typography overlays), (2) a redaction and synthetic-data policy for production screenshots, (3) a small Figma + CI export recipe and naming convention, (4) QA checklist and sample localized assets in three locales. This ticket scopes the design decisions, example assets, and handoff artifacts for Eng/Docs to implement automated exports and for Marketing to use in release collateral. Key constraints: keep screenshots truthful to product state while removing any customer or PII, support RTL/localization-safe cropping, and ensure assets are usable by non-designers.
ux_steps: Audit current onboarding screenshots used across quickstart and docs
Define crop/aspect presets: hero (16:9), modal (4:3), toolbar (1200x280), small card (3:2)
Create Figma file with components + overlay masks for safe area and redaction
Author redaction & synthetic-data policy and examples
Add automated export naming convention and per-locale suffix
Produce sample assets in en-US, fr-FR, ja-JP and RTL stub (ar-SA)
Create QA checklist and run through with PM/Legal/Eng
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with annotated templates and export presets available to Eng/Docs
Design spec includes explicit redaction rules and synthetic-data examples
CI recipe (docs repo) demonstrates automated export of 3 locales with correct filenames
Sign-off from PM and Legal on privacy rules
Publishable sample assets for hero, modal, and card sizes in at least 3 locales
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Kaur: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ONB/Visual+Asset+Guardrails. Initial audit found ~42 unique screenshots across quickstart paths; many include real emails and org names.

2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype presets pushed to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Onboarding-Screenshot-Templates. Started with 16:9 hero and 4:3 modal. Need guidance from Eng on responsive truncation.
2026-03-05 - PM feedback (Rhea Patel): Prefer smaller safe-area on mobile hero to retain readable UI. Also flagged that dedicated deployments show customer logos which must be masked by default.

2026-03-07 - Design decision: redact user identifiers by default and allow a 'synthetic' mode that swaps values for sanitized demo content. Trade-offs: synthetic data boosts clarity but may hide real UX edge-cases.
2026-03-08 - Eng comment (Danielle Wu): Automation note — automated cropping must not cut off token suggestion chips. We agreed to add a 64px horizontal safe margin for responsive states.

2026-03-10 - Legal review requested: uploaded privacy policy excerpt and redaction checklist. Legal to confirm redaction rule for hashed IDs. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1redaction-docs

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Added CI export recipe PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/425. Uses figma-export CLI and post-processing script to apply gaussian blur to masked regions and export localized frames.

2026-03-12 - Aisha Kaur: Ran initial QA pass. Found two modal states in ja-JP where line wrapping pushes controls into safe area — added note to 'responsive truncation' UX pattern and requested Eng adjust CSS or provide 'screenshot mode' class.
Follow-ups: legal sign-off on 2026-03-15, Eng to implement screenshot-mode hooks by 2026-03-16, design to finalize master Figma and deliver assets by 2026-03-18.
notes: This ticket avoids re-creating existing 'brand-safe-screenshot' work by focusing specifically on onboarding/quickstart flows (short guided tasks). The output must be consumable by Docs and Marketing with minimal design edits. Consider adding a lightweight 'screenshot-mode' CSS flag that increases margins and replaces real text with localized synthetic strings for safer automated captures.

Eng implement screenshot-mode hooks and responsive safe-area support (owner: Danielle)

Run CI export job and sanity-check localized assets (owner: Aisha)
